question: kit/07-QUALITY-BAR.md, R2, word for word
note: Each vote is one fresh agent that received one picture and the question of R2 and nothing else. The pictures carry neutral names; which judged frame each is stands in the key file, added when every answer is in. Each juror sent its one line to a clerk agent that saved it unchanged; the lines are read from those files by a script.

votes.why: the river surface has an unnaturally uniform, shader-like sheen.

the repeated scattered plant clumps and flat, uniform salt-crust textures look like a decent but ordinary scattered-asset 3D environment render (a paleo-art style landscape), not a photo or top-tier film frame.
the flat unreflective water surface with painted-looking white streaks and ungrounded reeds lacking contact shadows or reflections
The distant terrain looks like a flat plane painted with branching channels rather than banks with visible depth.
The scene is a clearly CG salt flat with repeated plant and rock assets and a smeared vertical streak in the haze at top right. Its detail and lighting are good but not film-grade.
the same dome shape repeats at different scales with nearly identical surface shading.
the domes have clean, uniform CG shading and the repeated plants look procedurally scattered. It reads as a competent but ordinary render, not a film-quality frame.
the rigid mesh-like burst bubble crown and kinked procedural plant stalks rendered with standard 3D lighting and depth of field
The distant vegetation repeats the same sharply angled, sparse frond shapes across the entire shoreline.

the fluid water simulation with a splash, salt crust, volumetric haze and detailed reeds look like high-end film or documentary CG, but the odd stylised dome shapes keep it from being clearly big-budget (c is the runner-up)
the near-identical red frond clusters look like copies of the same 3D asset.
polished but generic alien-plant scene with repeated plant models and plain foggy lighting, which looks like an ordinary 3D render rather than a top-budget cinematic
the flat CG lighting and simplistic procedural water with uniform foam rings around the bubbles
The foreground plants repeat the same ringed trunk and ribbon-like fronds like copies of a single 3D asset.

detailed fine-strand fronds and trunk texture with believable atmospheric haze, depth and water droplets point to high-end film/cinematic CG, though the alien subject (not a real place) and some slightly soft/uniform shading leave (c) as the alternative.
the smaller creature looks like a scaled-down copy of the main one, down to the silhouette and pose.

The creature skin is detailed but looks generic and procedural, and the ground looks flat and uniform with foggy, simple lighting. That reads as a good-quality personal or stock CG render, not film-grade compositing.
the flat unreactive water-to-body intersections and simple sculpted textures characteristic of an ordinary offline 3D render rather than a high-budget cinematic or real-time mobile engine
The smaller creature looks like a scaled-down copy of the larger one, right down to the skin folds.
the detailed skin texture, atmospheric fog depth and cohesive art direction on the alien creatures read as high-end film/cinematic CG (though some soft ground and plant detail leaves c plausible).
the water’s densely patterned ripples look procedural rather than naturally disturbed around the rocks.
alien salt-flat creatures with procedural-looking displacement textures and soft uniform lighting read as a polished but ordinary 3D render (e.g., a Blender/artist piece), not film-grade or a photo.
the blobby procedurally displaced rocks and simple whisker-like spikes intersecting the ground mesh without natural contact under standard CG overcast lighting
the foreground creature’s whiskers look like smooth tapered rods pushed into its textured skin.

The creature, salt crust and fine-grained surface detail with soft overcast lighting are very high-fidelity and cinematic, and the alien subject can't be a photograph. It could also be a polished solo-artist render (c).
